extracted.intended_audience: market participants, exchange members, and interested commenters on SEC SRO fee filings (e.g., MIAX members, broker-dealers, industry commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: A Securities Exchange Act rule filing by an exchange (MIAX Pearl Options) proposing changes to non-transaction fees (connectivity/port/certification fees), providing legal and economic justification, and soliciting public comment under the SEC notice-and-comment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with the Act (public solicitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may be submitted electronically via the Commission's internet comment form or by email (rule-comments@sec.gov), or by paper submission in triplicate to the SEC Secretary; include file number SR-PEARL-2024-05 on the subject line; use only one method to help processing efficiency; do not include personally identifiable information (the Commission may redact or withhold obscene or copyrighted material).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective filing and 60-day Commission suspension window
rubrics_metrics.description: The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act and Rule 19b-4(f)(2) thereunder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At any time within 60 days of the filing, the Commission may summarily suspend the rule change if it appears necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for investor protection, or in furtherance of the Act; if suspended, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments submission mechanics and public posting
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions should refer to file number SR-PEARL-2024-05 and should be submitted on or before March 1, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Commission's internet comment form (https://www.sec.gov/rules/sro.shtml) or send an email to rule-comments@sec.gov (include file number in subject), or send paper comments in triplicate to SEC Secretary at 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090. The Commission will post all comments on its website and make copies available in the Public Reference Room during official business hours. Do not include personally identifiable information; the SEC may redact or withhold certain material under 5 U.S.C. 552.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory standards for exchange rules (15 U.S.C. 78f(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchange rules (including fee schedules) are subject to statutory requirements under 15 U.S.C. 78f(b), including that rules be 'designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices', provide 'a fair procedure for the disciplining' of members, and not be 'designed to permit unfair discrimination'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing cites 15 U.S.C. 78f(b)(4) and 78f(b)(5) as applicable legal constraints when evaluating whether proposed fees are consistent with the Act; fees must be equitable and not unfairly discriminatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Staff Guidance and Revised Review Process to fee filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Staff Guidance on SRO Rule Filings Relating to Fees requires exchanges to provide improved disclosures and justify that their market data and access fee proposals are fair and reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Guidance served the policy goal of improved disclosures, the Exchange contends it has made it extraordinarily difficult for non-legacy exchanges to adopt or increase fees; the filing argues that exchanges must provide competitive and/or cost-basis rationale under the Revised Review Process and Staff Guidance and that staff has requested additional and detailed information (including confidential vendor cost data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-based approach disclosure and record development
rubrics_metrics.description: Under a cost-based standard, exchanges may be expected to disclose costs and supporting information sufficient to enable staff review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange provided detailed cost and revenue disclosures (some confidential) to Commission staff under separate cover and requested clearer guidance from staff about what constitutes an appropriate profit margin and what disclosures are required; the Exchange argues that, if a cost-based standard is to be applied, staff should indicate what they determine is an appropriate profit margin and require consistent disclosures across exchanges to ensure fair competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market-based vs. cost-based review and judicial precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission and courts have applied different standards in reviewing fee filings; e.g., the Commission historically applied a 'market-based' test in assessing market data fees, and court cases (Susquehanna; Nasdaq v. SEC; SIFMA decisions) affect available avenues to challenge fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The D.C. Circuit held Section 19(d) is not available to challenge generally-applicable fee rules (challengeable only if targeted); other cases and Commission orders (BOX Order, Susquehanna decision, SIFMA Decision) are referenced to explain the evolving standards and precedents relevant to fee filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntariness of Certification Logical Port fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Purchasing additional Certification Logical Ports, beyond the one free Certification Logical Port per logical port type offered in the production environment, is voluntary and not required to participate in production trading on the Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange defended the reasonableness of a $250 monthly Certification Logical Port fee by noting that at least one Certification Logical Port per type remains free and that similar fees are assessed by other exchanges (citing NASDAQ and MIAX filings); no market participant is required by regulation to purchase excess Certification Logical Ports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition and substitutability as justification for fees
rubrics_metrics.description: An exchange may justify fee proposals by demonstrating substitutable products and services are available to market participants (e.g., other options exchanges, third-party resellers, or OTC markets), and that demand would be met by competitors if an exchange exited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cboe argued proposed pricing more closely aligned access fees with affiliated exchanges and claimed substitutable connectivity and functionality exist; the Commission has stated that demand in the event of the exit of a competitor is likely to be swiftly met by existing competitors and that new entrants could create similar business models if demand were adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and transparency expectations across exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: For fair competition, exchanges should provide consistent and comparable disclosures in fee filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange contends it has produced extensive cost and revenue disclosures never previously disclosed by legacy exchanges and argues that detailed disclosures should be consistent across all exchanges (including those resisting a cost-based approach) to ensure fair and even disclosure and competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record availability and public inspection of filing materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the submission, subsequent amendments, written statements filed with the Commission, and communications between the Commission and any person related to the proposed rule change will be available for website viewing and in the Commission's Public Reference Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials (other than those withheld under 5 U.S.C. 552) will be posted on the SEC website; copies will also be available for inspection/copying at the Exchange's principal office. The filing instructs commenters not to include personally identifiable information in submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee schedule term definitions and their use in evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing includes definitions for technical and participant-related terms used in the fee schedule (e.g., 'Member', 'MEO Interface', 'Full Service MEO Port—Bulk', 'Limited Service MEO Port', 'Matching Engine', 'Affiliate', 'TCV', 'Market Maker', 'Electronic Exchange Member (EEM)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions determine applicability and calculation of fees and credits and are part of the evaluative record for whether fee proposals are equitable and not unfairly discriminatory; references to other exchanges' fee schedules and specifications (NASDAQ SQF, NYSE, etc.) are provided for comparison.
